headline: Critical Node-RED flaw exploited in attacks; Siemens IoT2050 backdoors and Synology NAS ransomware remain active

bullets.text: New: SecurityWeek reports a critical Node-RED flaw is being exploited in attacks.
The Hacker News reports attackers are exploiting a critical Siemens IoT2050 flaw, CVE-2026-58115, to plant remote command backdoors.
The Hacker News reports ransomware attacks on Synology NAS devices exploiting a patched DSM flaw.
Binance, 7 outlets: The Register reports the FBI pins the $6.3B heist on North Korean hackers. SecurityWeek says the FBI flagged over 600 addresses tied to it.

Connect Secure, 4 outlets: Ivanti patched two more zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13.
BleepingComputer reports over 1,000 GitLab servers are vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks. CISA KEV lists GitLab CE/EE flaw CVE-2026-97229, whose federal due date passed on 2026-11-01.

actions: Find Node-RED instances, check vendor guidance on the exploited flaw, patch, and take any internet-exposed ones offline until you have.
Find Siemens IoT2050 devices, check Siemens guidance on CVE-2026-58115, patch, and look for backdoors. Isolate any you cannot patch yet.
Update DSM on Synology NAS devices, restrict their internet exposure, and confirm backups are intact.
Patch GitLab CE/EE (CVE-2026-97229) and Cisco ASA/FTD (CVE-2026-76418) now; both KEV due dates have passed. Check GitLab servers for signs of RCE.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
If you handle crypto transactions, screen against the addresses the FBI flagged for the Binance heist.
